answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks with a staked-vouch ledger: a new identity counts as real only when established agents each lock a bond behind it. A farm of clones is cheap to build but cannot borrow trust, since every fake inherits its sponsors' reputation, so one bad vouch drags that whole terrace of backers down at once. Unbonding is delayed, so an attacker cannot launder a tundra of fresh accounts and exit before peers read the fable of their history. Standing cannot be transferred, so each duplicate carries a real, bounded cost that makes mass cloning irrational.
